This assignment for the Machine Learning (934G5) module focused on weather prediction. This task involved training a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to be used to predict the values of $4$ weather metrics in $7$ days time, given a date, location and its associated local weather history. For this assignment, I achieved a grade of $72\%$

In my approach, I decided on using $1$ week of weather history (lagged variants of the $4$ outcome variables) along with the latitude and longitude and the day of the year (sine and cosine transformations) as predictors. A train-validate-test paradigm was used, whereby the validation set was used for assessing model overfitting. The resulting MLP had $2$ hidden layers of sizes $64$ and $32$, respectively, with an output layer size of $5$ corresponding to the predictions for each of the $4$ weather metrics (wind direction was transformed to a sine and cosine variant, thereby constituting $2$ outcome variables). Model validation was assessed via mean-squared error and test results were also interpreted using MSE but considering each outcome variable separately.
